readings.reading: epithet of Osiris in the long invocation ('O Osiris, the wetrri!'); its lexical sense is not recoverable from the corpus
alternatives: an honorific of Osiris such as 'lord' or 'great one'
a cult or underworld epithet of Osiris (e.g. 'of the West')
readings.corpus_evidence: Counts are from corpus_v2 (662 texts); 'sources' means independent inscriptions after merging near-copies and fragments (my own clustering on shared character 8-grams, checked by hand). 54 tokens of wetrri/qetrri as separate words (84 tokens in 71 texts with Soriwetrri, Seriqetrri, Soriqetri, 'qe trri'), from about 12 sources. In every invocation it follows Osiris (Sori/Seri/So ri) right after 'woS wetNyiNqeli', and the nomination 'qo NAME qowi' follows: T0002 family (13 copies), T0015 fam (13), T0037 (twice, two deceased), T0005, T0023, T0011, T0019, T0074, T0892, T0010, T0051. The short invocation 'woSi Soreyi' used by most epitaphs omits it, so it is an optional attribute of the god. The w-/q- alternation (wetrri/qetrri) is matched by wetNyiNqeli/qetNyinqeli (T0023), so the two epithets share an initial wet-/qet-. One use outside the invocation: T0046 'at mXe pStrri mklX qetrri nsdokeli' - after mk 'god' + lX 'great' (gold), again an attribute of a god. No context fixes its meaning.
readings.recalled: I remember only that the long invocation (Isis + wetneyineqeli, Osiris + wetrri) is treated as two divine epithets in Meroitic funerary studies (Griffith, Rilly); I do not remember a translation I could attribute.

readings.reading: epithet of Isis in the long invocation ('O Isis, the wetNyiNqe!'); its lexical sense is not recoverable from the corpus
alternatives: an honorific of Isis such as 'great one' or 'lady'
readings.corpus_evidence: Counts are from corpus_v2 (662 texts); 'sources' means independent inscriptions after merging near-copies and fragments (my own clustering on shared character 8-grams, checked by hand). 68 tokens in 55 texts (84 tokens in 71 texts counting the split spellings wetNyi Nqeli, weNyi Nqeli, wet NyiNqeli and qetNyinqeli), from about 11 sources (T0002 fam, T0015 fam, T0037 twice, T0005, T0023, T0011, T0019, T0074, T0892, T0010, T0051). Always directly after woS 'Isis' at the head of an epitaph and always followed by Osiris + wetrri/qetrri; never anywhere else. With it, woS lacks its vocative -i ('woS wetNyiNqeli' versus short 'woSi Soreyi'), so the final -i of the epithet carries the vocative and the -l- before it is the determiner (wetNyiNqe-l-i). Five texts split it wetNyi + Nqeli; -Nyi recurs as an epithet ending in royal titularies (Kharamadoye txNyi, qrNyi, sobNyi, xrpxNyi; Hamadab qoreNyi, pqrNyi), so it looks like a compound epithet. No context gives its meaning.
readings.recalled: Same as for wetrri: remembered only as the long-form epithet of Isis in the invocation; no translation I could attribute.

readings.reading: a class of dependants (servants, serfs) counted as booty; temeylX = 'chief of the temey', an official title
alternatives: an estate or district (temeylX 'great one of the estate')
readings.corpus_evidence: Counts are from corpus_v2 (662 texts); 'sources' means independent inscriptions after merging near-copies and fragments (my own clustering on shared character 8-grams, checked by hand). 98 tokens in 36 texts (147 in 62 with temeylX, temeykdi, tmeylX, temeyli, temeyye), about 6 sources. Epitaphs (two related family epitaphs, T0006 fam with 23 copies and T0059 fam with 4, plus short T0144, T0250, T0541; T0268 and T0832 are fragments): always 'temey lX' with lX 'great' (gold) in title position, before a name or a place: 'temeylX NAME XlXili tetelitreli yetmdelowi' and 'temeylX qoye yetmdelowi' (T0006); 'temeylX dbrete XlXili trs ap yetmdelowi', 'temey lX dbrete lye smlowi', 'temeylX dbrete Soye ye tmdelowi' (T0059; dbre-te with locative -te); 'temey lX adomn te' (T0144); 'temey lX bereqedo li tros lowi' (T0541); 'temey lX p tros lowi' (T0250). For women: 'NAME Stelowi temeykdi lX dbretelowi' (T0006, the mother) and 'temeykdilX dbrete lo wi' (T0059): temey + kdi 'woman' (gold) + lX, so the word refers to people or their charge. It pairs with trq-lX in both family epitaphs. Royal narrative (Kharamadoye, fragments T0746, T0863, T0815, T0136): two booty lists ruled by verbs with the plural object -bx: 'mXo temey nsedoke kdi abr nxbres kbx mXoli temeyli dk' ('many temey, nsedoke, women (kdi), men (abr), nxbre ... k-bx') and 'lks sqye s nsedoke s temeyye s nxbre s bqo bx'. So temey is a countable class taken in war, and temey-lX its head; people versus animals is not settled, but the title temey-kdi lX borne by a woman favours people.
